turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted to O-lan that she would see the day when their eldest son would marry and that her wishes would be fulfilled.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked her husband if the eldest son had spoken to his bride and if the maid was happy with her new role in the family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he had spoken to his bride and that she was happy in her new role in the family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked her eldest son if he had shared her teachings with his bride and if she understood the importance of respecting her ancestors.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he had shared her teachings with his bride and that she understood the importance of respecting their ancestors.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked her eldest son if he had taken care of the necessary arrangements for the wedding and if everything was prepared.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he had taken care of the necessary arrangements for the wedding and that everything was prepared.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she felt a sense of relief and asked him to ensure the wedding was conducted with all the respect and dignity it deserved, for it was a momentous occasion for the family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would ensure the wedding was conducted with all the respect and dignity it deserved, and that he would do everything in his power to make her proud.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her son that she felt her time was short but was comforted by the thought of seeing him marry with the respect and ceremony she had always envisioned.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son assured his mother that he would make sure the wedding was a grand event, befitting her wishes, and that she would be proud of him.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her son that she must see him wed before she could rest, her voice firm yet tinged with a sense of urgency and the knowledge of her imminent departure.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he understood her wishes and would make sure the wedding preparations were completed as soon as possible to ensure she could see the ceremony.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her son and his wife that she would see them wed and then she must die, her words carrying the weight of her impending departure and the hope that her family would continue to thrive without her.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she would ensure the wedding preparations were carried out with the utmost care and respect, fulfilling O-lan’s wishes.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her family that she felt a growing sense of urgency to see her son wed, knowing that her time was short and her presence would bring comfort to the family in their transition.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan and Wang Lung that she would take care of every detail to ensure the wedding was a source of joy and comfort for them, even as they faced their sorrow.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would see to it that the wedding was a celebration of their family's love and unity, reassuring her that her wishes would be honored.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her family that she must see her son wed first, her voice firm yet tinged with the sorrow of her impending departure, urging them to prepare for the wedding without delay.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung reassured O-lan that they would make the wedding a joyful event, ensuring her son would be wedded soon as she wished, and his voice carried a mix of optimism and anxiety.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
